title: Investment Filter
equation: Deal Quality = People × Intentions × Rationale × Contracts
hook: The bigger the upside, the more tempted you'll be to skim the contract.
statement: Judge every opportunity on four things: good people, good intentions, good reasoning, and good contracts.
explainer: Character shows up in every future conflict. Hidden agendas cause misalignment. Honest people still make bad calls. And trust still needs structure. Big upside doesn't excuse a weak spot.
sop: Get clear on what they actually want out of it.
Check whether the business logic holds up.
Score People, Intentions, Rationale, and Contracts from 1 to 10.
Walk away if any one of them is weak.
equation_example: People 8, Intentions 7, Rationale 6, Contracts 3. 8 × 7 × 6 × 3 = 1,008 Deal Quality, out of 10,000. Higher means the deal can take some stress. If any one score is near zero, walk away, no matter how good the rest look.
question: Write down which of the four filters you're most likely to skip when the upside gets exciting.
closing_statement: One weak link can undo the other three.
caption:
Principle Nº 257: Investment Filter

The bigger the upside, the more tempted you'll be to skim the contract.

Judge every opportunity on four things: good people, good intentions, good reasoning, and good contracts.

Your turn: Write down which of the four filters you're most likely to skip when the upside gets exciting.
